text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Swiss seek "to make amends" over issue of Holocaust victims' accounts in Swiss banks.
- One dead, six hurt as Arab youth crashes car into Jerusalem store.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat "furious" at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delaying bid.
- Flu not fooled by high temperatures.
- Government to discuss blueprint for economic structural reforms today. Among proposals: Private buses, gas-station deregulation, third cell-phone operator.
- Government sets new taxes to pay for budget cuts.
- Water for industry to cost 32 percent more.
- 1996 withdrawals from provident funds at 12 billion shekels.
- Insurers: We'll cut premiums only if car thefts decline.
- Tadiran wins $35 million deal to supply Spanish army.
- Deficit reduction law passes narrowly in Knesset.
- Bezeq investments slashed by 16 percent.
- Teledata receives $7.2 million order.
GLOBES
- Treasury proposes retirement age for men 70, for women 65.
HAARETZ
- Arafat rejects Netanyahu proposal to put off date for completing the redeployment in the West Bank. Palestinian sources: Two leaders could meet today.
- Labour party delegates will vote today on manner in which party chairman will be selected.
- Since his appointment Education Minister Zevulun Hammer has yet to convene the advisory committee on Arab education.
MAARIV
- At the last moment the initialing of the Hebron agreement was again put off.
- Tension between Arafat and Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak.
- A new record: In December six cars were stolen in Israel each hour.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Rise of 8.6 percent in four days of trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in 1997.
- Elbit TV factory in Migdal Haemek halts production.
